bug_semantics: HPE OneView exposes PUT /rest/id-pools/executeCommand without authentication. The request JSON is deserialized as an ExecutableCommand; PoolController.executeCommand passes its attacker-controlled cmd property to RuntimeExecutorService.execute, which invokes Java Runtime.exec. A remote unauthenticated caller can therefore execute an arbitrary command (Rapid7 demonstrated a reverse shell as the trm3 Trusted RM Container user). Endpoint availability limits practical exposure: Rapid7 found it enabled on OneView for VMs 6.x and likely all unpatched OneView for HPE Synergy versions, while some other VM editions return 404 because ID Pools is disabled. HPE's official affected-products statement nevertheless lists all HPE OneView versions through 10.20.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable implementation is proprietary HPE OneView appliance code in guidserver.jar (com.hp.ci.mgmt.guidpools.controllers.PoolController plus RuntimeExecutorService), not code in rapid7/metasploit-framework. This repository contains a post-disclosure Metasploit exploit client and documentation only. The smallest true BIC would be the HPE source-history change that first combined unauthenticated reachability with execution of the request-controlled cmd value, but HPE's source repository and commit history are not public in the assigned evidence.
ai_marker: Not assessable: the true HPE OneView BIC commit object is unavailable, so there is no BIC author/committer identity or trailer block to inspect. No AI inference is made from the Rapid7 exploit commit a4dba967122de40dc3e4cba554dc4fa2be73ca48 because it post-dates disclosure and adds an exploit for the external flaw rather than introducing the vulnerable vendor code.
evidence: Vendor/version boundary: open https://support.hpe.com/hpesc/public/docDisplay?docId=hpesbgn04985en_us&docLocale=en_US and inspect HPESBGN04985 rev.4 (release date 2025-12-16, last updated 2026-01-31). Its affected-products section says 'HPE OneView - All versions through v10.20'; its resolution says v11.00 or later addresses the vulnerability and an updated security hotfix applies to versions 5.20 through 10.20, superseding the earlier Z7550-98077 hotfix. Mechanism/fix behavior: https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/ra-cve-2025-37164-analysis/ reproduces the decompiled NO_AUTH PoolController.executeCommand method, the attacker-controlled ExecutableCommand.cmd flow into Runtime.getRuntime().exec, a successful unauthenticated reverse-shell request, and the vendor hotfix's Apache rule `RewriteRule ^/rest/id-pools/executeCommand$ - [R=404,L]`. The earlier Rapid7 notice at https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-cve-2025-37164-critical-unauthenticated-rce-affecting-hewlett-packard-enterprise-oneview/ likewise identifies the endpoint, pre-11.0/5.20-10.20 boundary, and emergency binary hotfixes. Repository disambiguation (run in the assigned clone): `git log --follow --format='%H %P %aI %s' -- modules/exploits/linux/http/hpe_oneview_rce.rb` shows only a4dba967122de40dc3e4cba554dc4fa2be73ca48 and two same-day follow-ups; `git log --all --reverse --format='%H %P %aI %s' -S'executeCommand' -- modules/exploits/linux/http/hpe_oneview_rce.rb` returns a4dba967122de40dc3e4cba554dc4fa2be73ca48, parent 2bb30ba7a3eae4560a7e8ac34e09339804ddef2e, dated 2025-12-19, with subject 'add in the HPE OneView exploit'; `git log -L 143,157:modules/exploits/linux/http/hpe_oneview_rce.rb` shows that commit adding execute_cmd from /dev/null; and `git ls-tree -r --name-only 2bb30ba7a3eae4560a7e8ac34e09339804ddef2e -- modules/exploits/linux/http/hpe_oneview_rce.rb` is empty. `git show --format=fuller --stat a4dba967122de40dc3e4cba554dc4fa2be73ca48` shows a 404-line exploit/module-documentation addition after vendor disclosure, and `git describe --contains --tags a4dba967122de40dc3e4cba554dc4fa2be73ca48` returns `6.4.104~4^2~3`; these establish only the Metasploit exploit lifecycle, not a vulnerability BIC or vendor fix. Searching the clone for PoolController, RuntimeExecutorService, or com.hp.ci.mgmt.guidpools returns no vendor implementation. Thus no Git commit in this clone is the true introducer or direct fix, while the actual remediation is distributed by HPE as appliance release 11.00 and binary/config hotfixes rather than a public source commit.
reasoning: Vulnerability-first tracing places both causal components in HPE's closed appliance: an endpoint explicitly marked NO_AUTH and a controller/service path that executes the request body's cmd without an authorization or command-policy barrier. The revised hotfix closes the network path by forcing the endpoint to 404, and 11.00 is the first vendor-declared fixed release. The Rapid7 repository was linked by the advisory because it supplies exploit code; its earliest relevant commit landed three days after disclosure and its direct parent lacks the module, so treating that commit as the BIC would invert cause and proof-of-concept. Because neither the source change that introduced the HPE behavior nor the source change behind the vendor fix is publicly represented by a commit object, the smallest BIC, its immediate-parent absence, fix SHA, and BIC-only AI metadata cannot be established. This is a genuine proprietary-history boundary, so BLOCKED is more accurate than EVIDENCE_GAP and no NOT_AI/AI verdict is supportable.
remaining_gap: Blocked on non-public HPE OneView source/VCS history and commit objects for the vulnerable guidserver.jar implementation and the v11.00/hotfix remediation. Those records are required to identify the smallest true BIC, verify its immediate parent lacks the flaw, map the source-level direct fix, and inspect only the BIC commit object for AI authorship signals. Public appliance binaries and decompiled code prove behavior and release boundaries but cannot supply those commit-level facts.
